2. The claim, its estimand and its causal graph – the paper, the five analysts, and what the controls do

Work along in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), solo or in pairs, with the browser lab page as the fallback
:::

::: notes
Welcome – good to have you here. A full day, in four parts of ninety minutes. The first part sets up everything else: what we are doing when we do social science, why people say it is in crisis, what open research proposes to do about it, and the software without which none of it happens. The second part goes inside one published study, built on the European Social Survey, which asked whether Europeans who see immigration as a threat trust their national politics less, and asks what question its claim actually answers. In the third you reproduce a result that one of five independent analysts reported for that claim, and then vary the analysis yourself. And in the fourth we read what the class built, ask how sure sixteen countries let us be, and settle on the one analysis you would publish.
:::
